children.text: T2: Spaceships

Alice and Bob are twin astronauts approaching each other to reunite. Alice's spaceship moves towards Bob at \(u=3c/5\), where \(c\) is light speed. Each sends gifts to the other at regular intervals \(\Delta t_0\) measured in their own frame, with gift speed \(v=4c/5\) in that frame. Their separation \(L\) is large enough that many gifts are in transit at once.
a.i
In Bob's frame, find the distance between successive gifts sent by Alice.
a.ii
Find the interval \(\Delta t_1\) at which Alice's gifts arrive at Bob.
b
At one instant Alice sees gifts moving away from her and gifts moving towards her. Find the ratio of these two numbers.

statement.text:
T2: Spaceships
Alice and Bob are twin astronauts approaching each other to reunite. Alice's spaceship moves towards Bob at \(u=3c/5\), where \(c\) is light speed. Each sends gifts to the other at regular intervals \(\Delta t_0\) measured in their own frame, with gift speed \(v=4c/5\) in that frame. Their separation \(L\) is large enough that many gifts are in transit at once.
a.i
In Bob's frame, find the distance between successive gifts sent by Alice.
a.ii
Find the interval \(\Delta t_1\) at which Alice's gifts arrive at Bob.
b
At one instant Alice sees gifts moving away from her and gifts moving towards her. Find the ratio of these two numbers.

children.text: T2: Spaceships
a.i. Simultaneous separation in Bob's frame

Relativistic velocity addition gives gift speed \(w=(u+v)/(1+uv/c^2)=35c/37\) in the receiving frame. Successive emission events occur at the same place in Alice's frame, so Bob measures their interval as \(\gamma_u\Delta t_0\), with \(\gamma_u=5/4\). During that interval Alice moves by \(u\gamma_u\Delta t_0\), while the first gift travels \(w\gamma_u\Delta t_0\). Their simultaneous separation is
\[l_B=(w-u)\gamma_u\Delta t_0=\frac{16}{37}c\Delta t_0.\]

nodes.alt: Original two-emission diagram in Bob's frame: Alice moves by u times the dilated launch interval while the first gift moves by w times that interval. The distance between the two gifts is lB.

children.text: Alternatively, the spacing in Alice's frame is \(l_A=v\Delta t_0\). Boosting first to the gifts' rest frame gives proper spacing \(l_G=\gamma_vl_A\); boosting to Bob gives \(l_B=l_G/\gamma_w\). Here \(\gamma_v=5/3\), \(\gamma_w=37/12\), so the same \(16c\Delta t_0/37\) follows.
a.ii. Arrival interval
\[\Delta t_1=\frac{l_B}{w}=\frac{16}{35}\Delta t_0.\]

One may find the arrival interval first by intersecting successive gift worldlines with Bob's worldline and transforming the two arrival events. Their separation is at one place in Bob's frame, unlike the two emission events.

nodes.alt: Original spacetime diagram with Alice and Bob worldlines, gift emission interval Delta t0 and arrival interval Delta t1, and the arrival-event coordinates marked in both frames.

children.text: b. Gifts actually seen

Seeing is not a simultaneous inventory. Count the gift worldlines intersecting Alice's past light cone. Suppose Bob appears at distance \(d_B\) and lookback time \(t_l=d_B/c\). The oldest outgoing gift Alice still sees has apparent distance \(d_B+vt_l\). The newest visible incoming gift has apparent distance \(d_B-wt_l\). Therefore
\[N_\mathrm{out}\simeq\frac{d_B(1+v/c)}{v\Delta t_0},\qquad N_\mathrm{in}\simeq\frac{d_B(1-w/c)}{l_B},\]
\[\frac{N_\mathrm{out}}{N_\mathrm{in}}=\frac{1+v/c}{1-w/c}\frac{l_B}{v\Delta t_0}=18.\]
The large number of gifts makes endpoint and integer-count effects negligible. By symmetry the calculation can equally be done using Bob as observer.

nodes.alt: Original receiving-observer diagram distinguishing incoming gifts physically in transit from those visible after accounting for the light travel time.
Original sending-observer diagram: some gifts already received by the other ship remain visible in transit because news of their arrival has not yet reached the observer.

children.text: Graphical and imaginary-time alternatives

nodes.alt: Original past-light-cone diagram: outgoing gifts have slope 5/4, incoming gifts minus 37/35, and the observation light line slope minus one. Intersections at (4/9,-4/9) and (-8,8) give the count ratio 18.

children.text: With \(c=\Delta t_0=1\), Lorentz diagrams also give simultaneous spacing \(16/37\) and reception interval \(16/35\). The corresponding Alice-frame intersection coordinates are \((20/37,-12/37)\) for simultaneous Bob time and \((12/35,-20/35)\) for arrival. Applying \(t_B=(5/4)(t_A+3x_A/5)\), or the invariant interval, gives the same results.

nodes.alt: Original imaginary-time diagram with the Bob, Alice and gift axes, simultaneous separation L and emission and arrival intervals shown by triangle constructions.
Original imaginary-time observation diagram with both gift families and light reaching Alice, and segments AP and RQ whose ratio gives 18.

children.text: In the source's \(ict\) construction, \(\tan\alpha=-3i/5\), \(\tan\beta=-4i/5\), and \(\tan\gamma=-35i/37\). The sine rule gives the same spacings and intervals. For the visible count, the construction gives \(AP=(9/2)il\) and \(RQ=(1/4)il\), whose ratio is 18. A source intermediate spacing formula is labelled as a time interval, and one printed count-ratio denominator uses \(c-v\) instead of \(c-w\). The results above use the consistent event and velocity definitions. All original approaches and marking details remain in the PDF.

solution.text:
T2: Spaceships
a.i. Simultaneous separation in Bob's frame
Relativistic velocity addition gives gift speed \(w=(u+v)/(1+uv/c^2)=35c/37\) in the receiving frame. Successive emission events occur at the same place in Alice's frame, so Bob measures their interval as \(\gamma_u\Delta t_0\), with \(\gamma_u=5/4\). During that interval Alice moves by \(u\gamma_u\Delta t_0\), while the first gift travels \(w\gamma_u\Delta t_0\). Their simultaneous separation is
\[l_B=(w-u)\gamma_u\Delta t_0=\frac{16}{37}c\Delta t_0.\]

Alternatively, the spacing in Alice's frame is \(l_A=v\Delta t_0\). Boosting first to the gifts' rest frame gives proper spacing \(l_G=\gamma_vl_A\); boosting to Bob gives \(l_B=l_G/\gamma_w\). Here \(\gamma_v=5/3\), \(\gamma_w=37/12\), so the same \(16c\Delta t_0/37\) follows.
a.ii. Arrival interval
\[\Delta t_1=\frac{l_B}{w}=\frac{16}{35}\Delta t_0.\]
One may find the arrival interval first by intersecting successive gift worldlines with Bob's worldline and transforming the two arrival events. Their separation is at one place in Bob's frame, unlike the two emission events.

b. Gifts actually seen
Seeing is not a simultaneous inventory. Count the gift worldlines intersecting Alice's past light cone. Suppose Bob appears at distance \(d_B\) and lookback time \(t_l=d_B/c\). The oldest outgoing gift Alice still sees has apparent distance \(d_B+vt_l\). The newest visible incoming gift has apparent distance \(d_B-wt_l\). Therefore
\[N_\mathrm{out}\simeq\frac{d_B(1+v/c)}{v\Delta t_0},\qquad N_\mathrm{in}\simeq\frac{d_B(1-w/c)}{l_B},\]
\[\frac{N_\mathrm{out}}{N_\mathrm{in}}=\frac{1+v/c}{1-w/c}\frac{l_B}{v\Delta t_0}=18.\]
The large number of gifts makes endpoint and integer-count effects negligible. By symmetry the calculation can equally be done using Bob as observer.


Graphical and imaginary-time alternatives

With \(c=\Delta t_0=1\), Lorentz diagrams also give simultaneous spacing \(16/37\) and reception interval \(16/35\). The corresponding Alice-frame intersection coordinates are \((20/37,-12/37)\) for simultaneous Bob time and \((12/35,-20/35)\) for arrival. Applying \(t_B=(5/4)(t_A+3x_A/5)\), or the invariant interval, gives the same results.


In the source's \(ict\) construction, \(\tan\alpha=-3i/5\), \(\tan\beta=-4i/5\), and \(\tan\gamma=-35i/37\). The sine rule gives the same spacings and intervals. For the visible count, the construction gives \(AP=(9/2)il\) and \(RQ=(1/4)il\), whose ratio is 18. A source intermediate spacing formula is labelled as a time interval, and one printed count-ratio denominator uses \(c-v\) instead of \(c-w\). The results above use the consistent event and velocity definitions. All original approaches and marking details remain in the PDF.
